contents.text: How often should you replace the bearings on a CP-200?

The bearings on a CP-200 should be replaced every 32,000 operating hours. The intervals for bearings can be halved for pumps that handle abrasive liquids or run above 60 °C. The intervals for bearings are not specified for pumps that do not handle abrasive liquids or run below 60 °C.

CP-200 Centrifugal Pump Operating and Maintenance Manual › 7 Maintenance › 7.2 Service intervals
## 7.2 Service intervals
Inspect the mechanical seal and the bearings every 2,000 operating hours or six months, whichever comes first.
Replace mechanical seal PN-4471-B every 8,000 operating hours.
| Task | Interval |
|---|---|
| Inspect the mechanical seal and the bearings | 2,000 h or 6 months |
| Regrease the bearings (lithium-complex grease, 15 g per bearing) | 4,000 h |
| Check the coupling alignment | 12 months |
| Replace mechanical seal PN-4471-B | 8,000 h |
| Replace the bearings | 32,000 h |
Halve the intervals for pumps that handle abrasive liquids or run above 60 °C.

Replacing the CP-200 mechanical seal (training) › Replacing the CP-200 mechanical seal › Fitting PN-4471-C
## Fitting PN-4471-C
- Fit the cartridge without tilting it
- Don't mix PN-4471-B and PN-4471-C parts
The old torque of 22 N·m applied to PN-4471-B.

CP-200 Centrifugal Pump Operating and Maintenance Manual › 2 Description
# 2 Description
The CP-200 is a single-stage, end-suction centrifugal pump with a closed impeller, designed for clean or slightly contaminated water at up to 90 °C.
Two grease-lubricated ball bearings in the bearing housing carry the shaft.
A controller on the pump skid monitors the motor, the bearing temperatures and the seal-water pressure and trips the pump when a limit is exceeded.

CP-200 Centrifugal Pump Operating and Maintenance Manual › 9 Troubleshooting
# 9 Troubleshooting
The controller shows an error code for most faults; the CP-200 troubleshooting guide explains each code.
Table 9-1 Troubleshooting
|---|---|---|
| High bearing temperature | Too much or too little grease | Regrease as section 7.3 describes |
| Seal leaks steadily | Worn seal faces | Replace the mechanical seal (section 8.1) |
